draco_encoder_nodejs.js + draco_encoder.wasm -- vendored
https://www.npmjs.com/package/draco3d  (draco3d@1.5.7, tarball registry.npmjs.org/draco3d/-/draco3d-1.5.7.tgz)
author: Google Draco Team -- see LICENSE (Apache-2.0, fetched directly from
https://github.com/google/draco -- the tarball itself carries no LICENSE file, only
package.json's "license": "Apache-2.0" field)

Recorded at v4601.

*** A DIFFERENT BUILD WAS TRIED FIRST, AND IT HUNG INDEFINITELY. *** three.js r160's own
examples/jsm/libs/draco/draco_encoder.js (the natural sibling of vendor/draco/DRACOLoader.js's
decoder, and where a DRACOExporter.js-based encoder would have pulled its module from) was fetched
and tested directly: `DracoEncoderModule()`'s init promise never resolved, measured to over 100
minutes of pinned CPU on a real 3-vertex encode before being killed. Root cause not fully
diagnosed, but the file is internally asm.js-era Emscripten output (`"almost asm"` directive, no
`.wasm` file or `wasmBinary` reference anywhere, no `readyPromiseResolve`/`readyPromiseReject`
pattern) -- an old build shape, not the current one, and this sandbox's headless Chromium is not
where it was tested against. NOT vendored, and DRACOExporter.js (which needs that module as a
global) was never vendored either, since there was nothing working for it to call.

*** draco3d IS GOOGLE'S OWN CURRENT NPM PACKAGE FOR THIS, AND draco_encoder_nodejs.js IS
NODE-TARGETED, NOT BROWSER. *** Its own package.json test script is `nodejs
draco_nodejs_example.js` -- this build is routinely run in Node, unlike three.js's asm.js copy,
which was only ever exercised in a browser. Confirmed directly: `require()`'d in plain Node,
`createEncoderModule({})`'s promise resolved, and a real triangle round-tripped to a 75-byte
`DRACO`-magic buffer in milliseconds. RUNS IN NODE, so a gate can drive it the same way
tools/export/voxelGlb.mjs's own header already prefers ("no browser dependency") -- and unlike the
rejected build, no THREE.js Mesh/BufferGeometry is needed either: this talks to the low-level
Encoder/MeshBuilder API directly against raw position/index/normal/uv arrays, the same shape
tools/export/weldVertices.mjs already produces.

WHAT IS NOT VENDORED HERE, ON PURPOSE: draco_decoder_nodejs.js and draco_decoder.wasm (this
package's decoder half) -- vendor/draco/DRACOLoader.js already covers decoding, via a completely
different, smaller, pure-JS reimplementation (mrdoob/draco.js), and there is no reason to carry a
second decoder alongside it. draco3d.js itself (the tiny dispatcher this package wraps its two
halves in) -- a caller here only ever wants the encoder, so tools/export/dracoEncode.mjs requires
draco_encoder_nodejs.js directly.

EVIDENCE:
  - LICENSE reads "Apache License, Version 2.0" (fetched from google/draco's own repo root).
  - package.json (kept only long enough to read, not vendored) named "license": "Apache-2.0",
    "author": "Google Draco Team", "repository": "git+https://github.com/google/draco.git".
  - draco_encoder_nodejs.js locates its companion wasm via `__dirname + "/"` -- the two files
    must stay siblings in this directory, which is also why draco_encoder.wasm is binary and
    untouched rather than re-encoded or reformatted.
  - sha256 at time of vendoring: draco_encoder_nodejs.js
    8434adecd1446459601763e499be3697546056bca90b286a538ae0483a00845a; draco_encoder.wasm
    d2a3ac80c91980d5d321c116454834ff36264825c6d1794cc84e42288f158958.
